**Purpose & context**

Bernhard is working toward a fat loss goal of approximately 5 kg, targeting a sustainable 2-month timeline rather than rapid loss. His daily calorie target is 1,500–1,800 kcal with 150–200g of protein. He trains regularly (several times per week) and has a sedentary job. He has a solid muscle base, which means his metabolic rate runs somewhat higher than standard formulas suggest. His estimated TDEE places his chosen calorie range at a meaningful but not extreme deficit.

**Current state**

Bernhard tracks meals reactively — reporting what he's eaten rather than pre-planning full days — and prefers Claude to recalculate running totals and flag issues (protein too low, calories over ceiling) after each update. He's actively tracking daily intake across multiple days, with adjustments made in real time (e.g., portion corrections, swapping treats, reinstating or removing foods based on meal timing).

**Key learnings & principles**

- Protein target (150g+) is the primary constraint to watch; calories are secondary
- Standard BMR formulas may underestimate needs for muscular individuals — Bernhard's real-world ceiling is likely toward the higher end of his range
- Kefir works well as a pre-workout option when there's a long gap before an evening meal
- Portion discipline matters most with calorie-dense foods (pasta, chicken quantities, treats)

**Approach & patterns**

- Reactive tracking: Bernhard reports meals as eaten; Claude recalculates totals and flags deviations
- Prefers simple, minimal-cooking meals: protein pasta with tuna and tomato sauce, Skyr bowls with fruit, cottage cheese, canned tuna
- Wants variety — avoids leaning too heavily on any single protein source (e.g., doesn't want chicken every day)
- Occasional treats (wine gums, ice cream, cake) are accommodated within the daily budget with portion guidance
- Macro tables provided per meal alongside running daily totals

**Tools & resources**

- Regular foods in rotation: Clear Whey protein shakes, Kefir (3.5%), Skyr, cottage cheese, Hüttenkäse, canned tuna naturell, protein pasta (Eiweißnudeln), tomato-based sauces, chicken breast, mixed vegetables
- Meal prep option explored: high-protein pasta salad
